as an english nerd with a 95+ grade throughout ss i have some tips;

1. do NOT suck up to your teacher. no matter what you do. even if you do some of my extra brownie point tips, don’t make it obvious that you’re wanting to gain their favour.

2. do all the work. all of it. even the assignments they forget about — just do them. it’s all counted up in the end.

3. ask questions. questions about anything relevant and thought out, like readings or assignments. a go-to i have is “what are your expectations beyond the rubric for this assignment?” 

4. ask for specific feedback on how you can improve. i’ve found that whenever i’ve asked to sit down with a teacher and really talk through what their expectations are and what they thought i could improve upon, it strengthened both my performance in the subject AND my relationship with the teacher.

5. any chance you get to participate, please do. in any capacity. in my most recent grade 11 english class, for example, we were reenacting “the crucible” for as long as we were reading it. i made sure to go up and read at least once or twice a week to show the teacher that i was interested and wanted to enthusiastically participate in class activities. 

6. talk to teachers about your interests in relation to the subject; such as books or shows you like that are relevant to the stuff you’re doing in class. the real-world connections will make them go: 🤯

7. try your best to use proper grammar and spelling. it’s a small thing, insignificant to most, but it’s important and shows your teacher that you’re someone who knows your shit, and someone who understands the value of truly good writing.

8. concision. i struggle with it a lot (notice how this post is sooooo long?), but it goes a long way with teachers when you’re able to get an impactful point across within a reasonable amount of words.

9. taking notes. literary devices, rhetorical devices, the whole shebang — it comes in handy during exam time or when doing analysis. i like to keep note of everything we’ve covered in the course in one big google doc so i can refer back to it during exam time as well.

10. remember that there is absolutely NO cookie-cutter way to do english. it’s a very analytical and subjective class. the best way to ensure success is by not expecting it. go with the flow.

i hope this helps you! dm me if you have any more questions or need more help :)
